summary: Coming down the mountain, Jesus finds His disciples unable to free a boy from a violent spirit; He answers the father’s honest cry and sets the boy free.
key_insight: The father said, “if You can do anything.” Jesus turned the “if” back to him: “If you can believe.” The man’s reply, “Lord, I believe; help my unbelief!”, was faith mixed with doubt, and Jesus acted on it.
story: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, {Lk} Jesus found a great crowd around the other disciples, and scribes arguing with them. {Mk} As soon as the people saw Him, they were greatly amazed and ran to greet Him. He asked the scribes, “What are you discussing with them?” {Mk}

A man came and knelt before Him. {Mt} “Teacher, I implore You, look on my son, for he is my only child.” {Lk} A spirit had made the boy mute, and wherever it seized him it threw him down; he foamed at the mouth, gnashed his teeth and became rigid. “So I spoke to Your disciples, that they should cast it out, but they could not.” {Mk}

Jesus answered, “O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to Me.” {Mt} When the boy saw Jesus, the spirit at once threw him into a convulsion, and he fell on the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth. {Mk}

Jesus asked the father, “How long has this been happening to him?” “From childhood,” he said. The spirit had often thrown him into the fire and into the water to destroy him. “But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.” Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.” Immediately the father cried out with tears, “Lord, I believe; help my unbelief!” {Mk}

Seeing the crowd come running together, Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit: “Deaf and dumb spirit, I command you, come out of him and enter him no more!” The spirit cried out, convulsed the boy terribly and came out. He lay so still that many said, “He is dead.” But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and he arose. {Mk} Jesus gave him back to his father, and they were all amazed at the majesty of God. {Lk}

Later, in the house, the disciples asked Him privately, “Why could we not cast it out?” {Mk} “Because of your unbelief,” Jesus said. If they had faith as a mustard seed, they could say to this mountain, “Move from here to there,” and it would move. {Mt} “This kind can come out by nothing but prayer and fasting.” {Mk}
differences: Only Luke says this happened “the next day” and that the boy was the man’s only child; only Mark describes the scribes arguing with the disciples.
Matthew says the boy “is an epileptic” and has the father kneel; Mark speaks of “a mute spirit” and records Jesus’ command, “Deaf and dumb spirit.”
Only Mark records the father’s “if You can do anything,” his tearful cry, and the boy lying as if dead.
Matthew gives the disciples’ failure as “Because of your unbelief” and adds the mustard seed; Mark gives “prayer and fasting.” Some manuscripts lack “and fasting” in Mark, and lack Matthew 17:21.

fit.question: Why could the disciples not cast the spirit out? Matthew says it was their unbelief; Mark says this kind comes out only by prayer.

points.label: Root and remedy
points.text: Prayer is faith turning to God. The disciples had cast out demons before (Mark 6:13) and may have come to treat that power as their own. Jesus names the root of their failure, unbelief, and the remedy, dependent prayer.

points.label: One conversation
points.text: In the NKJV, Matthew records both answers: unbelief (17:20) and prayer and fasting (17:21). Each writer reports part of the same private conversation in the house.

fit.note: The two Gospels give two sides of one answer; in Jesus’ teaching, faith and prayer are never rivals.
fit.short: Unbelief was the root; prayer was the remedy. Matthew and Mark record two sides of one private answer.

scene.label: Below the mountain
scene.text: While Peter, James and John saw Jesus’ glory, the other nine faced a crowd, critics and a suffering child. Moses, too, came down from the mountain of God to find failure in the camp below (Exodus 32:15–19).

scene.label: “An epileptic”
scene.text: Matthew’s word literally means moonstruck, a common term for seizures in that day. The Gospels describe the symptoms but say plainly that a spirit caused them here. They do not treat every illness this way: Matthew 4:24 lists the demon-possessed and epileptics separately.

scene.label: A mustard seed
scene.text: The mustard seed was the smallest seed a Galilean farmer sowed and a common picture of something tiny (Matthew 13:31–32). Moving a mountain was a picture of doing what seems impossible (compare 1 Corinthians 13:2).

witnesses.matthew: Tells the healing briefly and spends his attention on the disciples’ question afterward, “Why could we not cast it out?” With the mustard seed saying, the scene becomes a lesson in faith for Jesus’ followers.
witnesses.mark: Gives by far the fullest account: the arguing scribes, the boy’s symptoms, the father’s “if You can do anything” and his tearful cry. Mark alone shows the boy lying like a dead man until Jesus takes his hand and lifts him up.
witnesses.luke: Notes that the boy was an only child and that Jesus “gave him back to his father,” as He once gave a widow’s only son back to his mother (Luke 7:12–15). Luke ends with everyone amazed “at the majesty of God.”

seeing.reveals: Jesus is grieved by the unbelief all around Him, yet He gives His full attention to one father and one son. He commands a spirit with authority, “enter him no more,” and takes a boy by the hand with tenderness.
seeing.living: Jesus did not wait for this father to have perfect faith. Bring Him the faith you have, mixed with doubt, and ask Him to help your unbelief. When past success tempts you to rely on yourself, return to dependent prayer.
seeing.ponder: Can you pray honestly today, “Lord, I believe; help my unbelief!”? What would you bring to Him with that prayer?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus meets weak faith that cries out to Him, and does what we cannot.
outline: A crowd, a child and a failure (14–18)
A faithless generation and a patient Lord (19–22)
A boy raised and a lesson in prayer (25–29)
preaching.watch_for: Mark sets this scene right after the Transfiguration. Glory on the mountain gives way to helplessness in the valley, and the question shifts from what Jesus can do (“if You can”) to what the father will believe.
related_other: Exodus 32:15–19 · Moses comes down to failure
